tts_summary: Here's what you need to know about Meta's third quarter earnings report. The headline read is modest upside on revenue and healthy upside on operating income, with the core advertising business continuing to fire. Revenue came in at $64.6 billion, up 26% year-over-year, beating the Street's $63.3 billion estimate. The growth was driven by ad impressions up 10% and price per ad up 14% — both metrics moving in the right direction simultaneously, which is the ideal combination for an ad-driven platform. On operating income, excluding a nearly $10 billion one-time charge, Meta generated $22.88 billion versus the $20.8 billion consensus. That's meaningful upside. Free cash flow also beat significantly — negative $2.12 billion versus a Street estimate of negative $8.9 billion — but Adam flags this as a capex timing issue rather than a sign of spending restraint. In fact, the full-year capex guide was nudged higher to a range of $135 to $145 billion from the prior $130 to $145 billion range, so they are not pulling back on investment. The one soft spot was user metrics — daily active people came in at 3.64 billion, just under the 3.66 billion consensus, a small but notable miss. Looking ahead, Q4 revenue guidance midpoint lands at $74.5 billion, roughly $1 billion above where the Street was sitting, and management said they expect to sustain strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027. On the capital structure front, the board approved a new Class C non-voting share structure with an effective date in January 2027. There had been chatter heading into earnings that Meta might launch a big equity offering — the Class C move is a step in that direction, but nothing concrete is expected until next year if it happens at all. The bottom line here is that the core ads business is healthy, AI investments appear to be generating real incremental advertising revenue, and guidance is ahead of expectations. The capex story remains a spending commitment, not a pivot. Net net, this print reads as modestly positive for the stock.
